Functional groups, pKa, and the form you meet at pH 7.4

120 original reference groups, updated with aqueous pKa or pKaH values where useful. Ionizable structures are drawn in a representative dominant form at physiological pH.

Carbon skeletons & oxygen groupsHalogens, nitrogen & sulfur groupsMore sulfur, phosphorus & aromatic ringsFused & saturated ringsShorthand in papersSMILES guideSources
pKa is for an acid

The pH where HA and A⁻ have equal concentrations. Below pKa, protonated HA becomes more common; above pKa, A⁻ does.

pKaH is for a base's conjugate acid

The pH where BH⁺ and B are equal. Below pKaH, BH⁺ becomes more common; above pKaH, B does.

Read the numbers as reference points

Values refer to water, generally near room temperature. Substituents, neighboring groups, ionic strength, and local environment can shift them.

SOURCE PAGE 6 / 6

How to read SMILES

Six rules cover most of the notation in this reference.

1. Letters are atoms

C, N, O and S are elements; F, Cl, Br and I are halogens. Hydrogens are usually implicit.

CCO = ethanol

2. Neighboring atoms are bonded

A single bond needs no symbol. = is double and # is triple.

CC=O = acetaldehyde

3. Parentheses are branches

Text in parentheses hangs off the preceding atom.

CC(=O)O = acetic acid

4. Matching digits close rings

The two atoms with the same digit are bonded to each other.

C1CCCCC1 = cyclohexane

5. Lowercase means aromatic

c is aromatic carbon. An aromatic nitrogen carrying H is written [nH].

c1ccncc1 = pyridine

6. Brackets show details

[N+], [O-] and [n-] show charge. A dot separates unconnected components; @ marks stereochemistry.

C[N+](=O)[O-] = nitromethane
Putting it together

O=C(Nc1ccc2c(c1)OCO2)c1cc(F)c(F)c(F)c1F

An amide links a benzodioxole-containing ring to a tetrafluorophenyl ring. In the group cards, * denotes an attachment point and R represents the rest of the molecule.

Sources and interpretation

Values tagged [W] come from an aqueous compilation; [E] and [B] provide supporting class and heterocycle values. [R] and [S] support specific sulfur-group examples. Drug values come from compound records and literature. A range on a generic R-group card is illustrative, not a prediction for every derivative.

  • [W] Williams aqueous pKa compilation (ACS Organic Division)
  • [E] Evans and Ripin pKa tables (ACS Organic Division)
  • [B] Baran and Richter, Essentials of Heterocyclic Chemistry
  • [R] Nyasse et al., aqueous pKa of substituted sulfonamides
  • [S] Escher et al., ionization of organic chemicals in water
  • [P] PubChem compound records (NIH)
  • [C] Benzimidazole ligand study: reference aqueous pKaH table
  • [Y] PubChem: 2-pyrrolidone aqueous pKa, citing IUPAC acid constants
  • [N] NCBI Bookshelf: Paracetamol
  • [J] Acetylsalicylic acid biowaiver monograph

The structures are adapted from the supplied PDF. Where a charge label was changed, the SMILES beneath the card was changed to match. The original PDF's instructional text was treated as reference content, not as instructions for this work.
